subject: Teruaki Sato
title: Teruaki Sato Cubs: How big is his deal? 6 years, $120 million
answer: Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato has agreed to a six-year, $120 million contract with the Chicago Cubs, ESPN's Jeff Passan reported on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026, with MLB.com, The Athletic and CBS Sports confirming the terms through sources. The Cubs had not announced the deal.
in_the_news: Sato, the 2026 Triple Crown winner for Japan's Hanshin Tigers, was one of the top free agents of the winter, and the deal tops an early Sports Illustrated estimate of about $100 million. It lands a week before baseball's labor agreement expires on Dec. 1.
body:
Sato, who bats left-handed, hit 39 home runs with 106 RBIs and a batting average above .300 in 2026, becoming the first Triple Crown winner in Japan since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. He was the Central League MVP in 2025 and has played mostly third base, with significant time in the outfield. The Philadelphia Phillies, Texas Rangers, Arizona Diamondbacks and New York Mets were among the teams reported to be in the bidding; the Cubs were described as still "in the mix" only a day before the agreement.

The deal continues an active Cubs offseason, CBS Sports noted, and it is bigger than the contracts two recent Japanese hitters received: the Cubs signed outfielder Seiya Suzuki for five years and $85 million in March 2022, while the Boston Red Sox gave Masataka Yoshida five years and $90 million in December 2022.

How posting works, in plain words: a Japanese player under team control can only come to MLB if his club "posts" him. That opens a 45-day window to negotiate with all 30 teams. Whoever signs him also pays his old club a release fee: 20% of the first $25 million of the contract, 17.5% of the next $25 million and 15% of everything above $50 million. On a $120 million deal, that works out to roughly $19.9 million for Hanshin, on top of what Sato is paid. This year the clock was tighter than usual: USA Today and The Athletic reported in early November that MLB would not pause posting windows if a lockout begins when the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, which pushed posted players to sign before that date.

What comes next: the agreement becomes official after Sato passes a physical and the Cubs announce it. Two other Japanese players posted the same week, pitchers Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh, are still on the market, and The Athletic reported the Cubs have also shown interest in Taira.

faq.q: How much will the Cubs pay to the Hanshin Tigers?
faq.a: Under the MLB–NPB posting formula, a $120 million contract means a release fee of about $19.9 million, paid separately from Sato's salary.

faq.q: What position will Teruaki Sato play?
faq.a: He played mostly third base in Japan and also has extensive outfield experience. The Cubs have not said where he will line up.

faq.q: Is the Teruaki Sato deal official?
faq.a: Not yet. It was reported by ESPN and confirmed by several outlets through sources, but it is pending a physical and an announcement by the team.

faq.q: Why was there a rush to sign Japanese players before Dec. 1?
faq.a: Baseball's labor deal expires on Dec. 1, and MLB said posting windows would not be paused during a lockout, according to USA Today and The Athletic.
